newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed says Yeltsin still sick, should resign.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says Yeltsin still sick, should resign.

text.p: Former Russian security chief and presidential aspirant Alexander Lebed was quoted on Friday as saying President Boris Yeltsin was still a sick man despite heart bypass surgery and urged the Kremlin leader to resign.
"I know perfectly well that Boris Nikolayevich Yeltsin is a very ill person," Lebed told the Nezavisimaya Gazeta daily newspaper in an interview.
He accused some presidential aides of ruling Russia behind Yeltsin's back. "This man is now being manipulated in a most impudent way," he said.
"The president's resignation would be a normal, civilised way out of the situation," Lebed added. "He should resign for health reasons."

Yeltsin, who has a history of heart problems, says he feels well and full of energy after his operation on November 5. He returned to his Kremlin office on Monday after almost seven weeks of recuperation.
Pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who advised Yeltsin before and during the Moscow operation, has said the 65-year-old Russian leader can expect at least 10 more years of active work.
Debakey said earlier this week Yeltsin was capable of working eight hours a day now and would be able to do more with time.
Lebed, a former paratroop general who openly declares his ambitions to become president, chaired a meeting on Friday of his Dignity and Motherland political movement.
There he called on Yeltsin to hand over some of his powers to ensure a smooth transition of power.
"This would create a favourable political atmosphere for his departure from big politics," Interfax news agency quoted Lebed as saying.

"We view as appropriate a constitutional reform which would transform the existing super-presidential republic into a normal republic run by president and parliament," Lebed told members of his movement.
Lebed, who came a solid third in a first round of voting in presidential elections last June, later backed Yeltsin in the run-off on July 3 to defeat a strong communist contender.

But the alliance, which brought Lebed appointment as Yeltsin's national security adviser and secretary of his policy-making Security Council, collapsed in October when the former general fell out with the Kremlin elite.
Yeltsin sacked Lebed dramatically, accusing him of having no team spirit and flagrant presidential ambitions.
Lebed told his supporters that presidential powers should be limited to naming prime minister, directing foreign policy and controlling the country's defence, interior and security forces.

"The real control of social and economic development of the country should belong to the government responsible to parliament's lower house and formed according to the results of parliamentary elections."
Communists and their supporters dominate the State Duma lower house.
